A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VEAttack research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioning, VQA, hallucination, transfer-attack and ablation experiments, plus classification evaluations and qualitative examples in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds retrieval, visual grounding, joint LLM attacks, and further transfer and perceptual analyses.

M1.justification: The main patch-token cosine-similarity attack in Eq. (7) remains unchanged. Appendix E adds an auxiliary VEAttack+LLM variant that jointly supervises LLM hidden states, extending the attack objective for an ablation. Renaming the main setting gray-box does not change its access requirements or procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds image-text retrieval on Flickr30k and visual grounding on RefCOCO and RefCOCO+ in Appendices G–H. These introduce ranking and spatial-localization tasks beyond the retained coverage. OK_VQA, additional captioning metrics and the twelve classification datasets were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces Lcls and L2 with VT-Attack and AttackVLM-ii, while retaining MIX as MIX.Attack; Lcls and L2 remain in appendix comparisons. v2 also adds FOA-Attack in Figure 2, QAVA in the extended captioning table, SGA/DRA in retrieval, and AnyAttack/M-Attack in perceptual comparisons. This substantially expands the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported non-CLIP transfer step size from 4/255 to 16/(255×5) and specifies 1000-step MIX.Attack/VT-Attack comparisons, versus v1's general 100-step setting. New protocols include retrieval ASR@1/10 and resource measurements, grounding on TestA/TestB/Val, and a 1000-image COCO transfer evaluation. Figure 2 also changes its cross-model comparisons to joint task/model transfer. These reported changes do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a joint vision-encoder/LLM ablation, feature-deviation trajectories across transfer settings, failure analysis for transfers from specialized larger encoders, and perceptual comparisons using images, L2 distances and CLIP similarities. These investigate efficiency, transfer mechanisms and perceptibility beyond v1's retained token-target, loss, iteration and budget analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Additional sample counts and averages in v2 do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains VEAttack's raw attack scores but changes some POPE clean/MIX values and adds comparator results. Table 2 replaces transfer scores and changes rankings: for the CLIP-backed LLaVA target, TeCoA/FARE source scores change from 61.3/47.6 to 22.1/38.7. Numerous new results appear in Tables 7 and 9–13 and the perceptual analyses. Transfer-score changes accompany revised reported settings and should not be interpreted as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–2, their assumptions, bounds and detailed derivations are retained. The proofs move from Appendices A–B to B–C, with terminology and formatting changes rather than substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The central vision-only, task/label-agnostic contribution, 94.5%/75.7% degradation claims and four observations remain. v2 adds a 13-fold runtime-reduction claim against VT-Attack alongside the retained eight-fold Ensemble comparison. Gray-box terminology clarifies the existing access setting rather than introducing a new capability.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive mechanism explanations: robust encoders supposedly force more transferable semantic disturbances, while specialized encoder feature spaces explain weak cross-model transfer. Appendix E interprets joint LLM attacks as offering limited benefit at substantial computational cost. These extend v1's interpretations and applicability boundaries; the unresolved defense limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 updates the stated repository location and adds a reproducibility statement describing supplementary code, a README and run scripts. Appendix A also describes a planned research-restricted release of code and adversarial examples. These expand documented access information; the PDFs alone do not verify the resources' availability.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions VEAttack within a white-box/black-box/gray-box taxonomy and distinguishes it from existing visual-feature attacks using text information or additional encoders. New discussion and citations include VT-Attack, QAVA, FOA-Attack, M-Attack, CroPA and Doubly-UAP. This changes the comparison with prior research beyond citation-style updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, attack-related work and motivation are substantially rewritten around the gray-box positioning. Terminology changes throughout, including image tokens to patch tokens. New reproducibility, ethics, responsible-disclosure and LLM-use statements expand the document structure, while the main methodology sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 redraws attack illustrations and Figure 2, including new comparison groups and a degradation-rate axis. It adds feature heatmaps, encoder-distribution and perceptual-comparison figures, several experimental tables, and restructures Table 3. Table 1 changes drop annotations to percentages. Existing caption/VQA example figures are retained as Figures 12–13, and the document adopts conference formatting.

improvement.justification: Relevant gray-box comparators, retrieval/grounding evaluations and the joint-LLM ablation make the central generalization and efficiency claims better assessable than in v1. However, new reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: Appendix F claims consistent superiority and cites scores absent from Table 9, where MiniGPT-4 CIDEr actually favors AttackVLM-ii, 5.4 versus VEAttack's 10.0. Section 5.3 also retains numerical summaries inconsistent with revised Table 2. The evidential expansion is useful, but reporting reliability remains uneven.
